node-1.label: An 81-year-old man presented with cough, fever, shortness of breath, and later developed right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with a miotic right pupil.

node-2.label: An 81-year-old man with medical history of coronary artery disease with coronary artery bypass two years prior, atrial fibrillation on rivaroxaban, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c 8.1%).

node-3.label: Initially developed cough, subjective fever, and shortness of breath; was treated with azithromycin for bronchitis, then levofloxacin after a right upper lobe infiltrate was found; symptoms progressed despite antibiotics.

node-4.label: Exposure history: spent time at a Northern Minnesota cabin with minimal outdoor exposure; previous missionary work in Colombia ended two years before admission; never smoked and rarely consumed alcohol.

node-5.label: Physical exam: temperature 38.6°C, pulse 130 beats/min irregularly irregular, blood pressure 114/61 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 82% improving to >90% with 5 L/min oxygen; diminished lung sounds in right upper lobe and diffuse crackles in right lung base; systolic ejection murmur, mild pitting edema to knees bilaterally; no clubbing, cyanosis, cervical/axillary lymphadenopathy; neurologic and skin examinations normal.

node-6.label: Later developed right-sided ptosis and anisocoria with asymmetrically miotic right pupil, more evident in dark environment.
